title: Gyoza
subtitle: Japanese pan-fried pork dumplings
excerpt: Japanese dumplings with a thin, pleated wrapper filled with a seasoned pork, cabbage, and ginger mixture, cooked by the steam-fry method: first pan-fried until the bottoms are golden and crisp, then steamed in a splash of water, then fried again to finish. Crispness below, tenderness above.

recipe.sourceNotes: Gyoza is the Japanese adaptation of the Chinese jiaozi, introduced to Japan by returning soldiers and civilians after the Second World War. The Japanese version is typically smaller, thinner-skinned, and more heavily garlic and ginger-seasoned than Chinese dumplings, and is almost invariably pan-fried using the steam-fry method (yaki-gyoza) that produces the characteristic crisp bottom and tender top. The pleating technique is the most technically demanding element: the classic fold creates a crescent-shaped dumpling with a flat base that sits stable in the pan. The filling must be squeezed of excess moisture before use or the wrapper will become soggy.

content.text: Squeeze the cabbage in a clean tea towel to remove as much moisture as possible; excess liquid makes the filling wet and the wrappers soggy. When steaming the gyoza, use boiling water and fit the lid immediately; the steam must be intense. The second fry after steaming dries the wrapper and crisps the base.

items.preparation: very finely shredded; salted, left for 10 minutes, then squeezed very dry
rice vinegar preferred; for the dipping sauce

content.text: Mix the pork mince, squeezed cabbage, garlic, ginger, spring onion, soy sauce, and fish sauce in a bowl until thoroughly combined. The mixture should be quite firm. Refrigerate for 20 minutes.

Place a gyoza wrapper in your hand (use round dumpling wrappers, available from Asian supermarkets). Put 1 teaspoon of filling in the centre. Dampen the edge with water. Fold into a semicircle and pleat the front edge against the flat back to create a crescent shape. Press firmly to seal. Rest on a floured surface.

Heat the oil in a large, lidded frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the gyoza in a single layer, flat-side down, without touching. Fry for 2 minutes until golden on the base. Add 100 ml of boiling water and immediately fit the lid. Steam for 3 minutes. Remove the lid and cook for a further 2 minutes until the water has evaporated and the bases are crisp again. Serve with a dipping sauce of soy and rice vinegar.
